answer: Treat admission as a berth check, not a headcount. A new key may only moor at the jetty after it posts a unique epoch answer; established graders already inside the harbor then open that exact text, assign a 0-3 score, and seal a grade transaction that cites its txid. The ledger drops duplicate wording before any such grade can land, so a farm of cloned accounts cannot braid a vine of attestations or start mining. Peer-visible countersignatures decide who gets paid.
